title: The 10 Best Cordless Framing Nailers
subtitle: Battery-powered framing nailers for decks, sheds and remodels, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Cordless framing nailers drive 2 to 3-1/2 inch nails without a compressor, hose or gas cartridge. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita, Metabo HPT and CRAFTSMAN on rating, review volume and features (a battery in the box, a light tool body and a warranty of three years or more). The first decision is the nail angle: 21° nailers take plastic-strip nails, 30° nailers take paper-tape nails.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: Metabo HPT 18V MultiVolt Cordless 21° Framing Nailer Kit (NR1890DRA)
products.best_for: Framers buying into a cordless nailer from scratch who want the lightest tool here.
products.verdict: A complete kit with a 4.0Ah battery and charger. The listing quotes 120 joules of driving power, about 500 nails per charge and 8.4 lb without the battery, and Metabo HPT covers the tool body for life.
cons: About 500 nails per charge on the included battery

products.name: Metabo HPT 18V MultiVolt Cordless 21° Plastic Strip Framing Nailer Kit with 4.0Ah Battery (NR1890DRST)
products.best_for: Buyers who want a battery-included 21° kit for less than the newer NR1890DRA.
products.verdict: Metabo HPT's earlier 21-degree cordless framer, still sold as a kit with a 4.0Ah battery. The listing claims about 600 nails per charge and 2 nails per second, with a lifetime tool warranty.
cons: 2 nails per second, slower than the newer models

products.name: Metabo HPT 18V Paper Tape Cordless Framing Nailer, 30° Kit (NR1890DCA)
products.best_for: Framers who use 30° paper-tape nails and want a complete kit.
products.verdict: The 30-degree twin of the NR1890DRA: brushless, 8.2 lb without the battery, up to 3 nails per second with no ramp-up time, and a battery, charger and lifetime tool warranty in the box.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Framing Nailer, 21 Degree, up to 3-1/4 inch Nails, Tool Only (CMCN621PLB)
products.best_for: CRAFTSMAN V20 owners building decks, sheds and additions.
products.verdict: A 21-degree framing nailer for CRAFTSMAN V20 owners that the listing says will drive 3-1/4 inch round head nails into LVL. It has tool-free depth adjustment, a rafter hook and a 3-year warranty.
pros: Drives up to 3-1/4 in nails into LVL

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL 30 Degree Framing Nailer, Tool Only (2745-20)
products.best_for: Milwaukee M18 owners who frame with 30° nails.
products.verdict: The most-reviewed cordless framing nailer here, sold under the Milwaukee brand. The listing is bare: the model number and not much else.
cons: Listing lists no weight or nail range

products.verdict: The best seller here: DEWALT's current 30-degree framing nailer as a bare tool for 20V MAX owners. The listing itself says almost nothing beyond the model and weight.
pros: 600+ sold last month, the most here
Uses 30° paper-tape nails, common at lumber yards

products.verdict: The DCN930 sold as a kit with a battery and charger, for anyone who isn't on DEWALT 20V yet. Like the bare-tool listing, it gives almost no detail beyond the model.

products.verdict: The 21-degree version of DEWALT's framing nailer, for plastic-collated full round head nails. It sells well but rates lower than the 30-degree model.

avoid.name: Milwauke M18 FUEL 21-Degree Framing Nailer (Tool Only) New
avoid.flag: Third-party listing with a misspelled brand and no specs
avoid.verdict: This listing sells a Milwaukee 2744-20 under the brand 'cakuuma' with the maker spelled 'Milwauke', and its bullets are generic company boilerplate with no specs. Buy a Milwaukee-branded listing instead.
reasons: The brand field says 'cakuuma' and the title and manufacturer field both spell the maker 'Milwauke', so it's unclear who is selling it or whether Milwaukee's warranty applies.
None of the five bullets describe the nailer: they're generic praise for the company ('is dedicated to delivering a steady stream of advanced solutions') with the brand name missing.
It lists no nail range, angle details, modes or warranty, which you need to match a nailer to your nails.

buyers_guide.a: It comes down to the nails you can buy locally and your building code. 21° nailers take plastic-strip full round head nails. 30° (and 30-34°) nailers take paper-tape nails, usually clipped head, and the magazine is shorter so it fits between studs more easily. Check that full round head nails aren't required where you build before going 30° with clipped heads.

buyers_guide.q: Are cordless framing nailers as good as pneumatic?
buyers_guide.a: For decks, sheds, remodels and punch-out work, yes: no compressor, no hose, and the better ones fire 2 to 3 nails per second. Full-time production framers still tend to use pneumatic because the tools are lighter and never need charging.
A cordless framer carries its own motor and drive system, so most weigh 8 to 11 lb before you add the battery. The Metabo HPT kits are the lightest here at 8.2 to 8.4 lb.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy the bare tool or a kit?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own batteries on the same platform, buy the bare tool and use your largest battery. If not, a kit is usually the cheaper way in than buying a bare tool, battery and charger separately.
The listings here claim about 500 to 1,100 per charge, depending on the battery. Use a 4.0Ah or larger battery for framing; small compact packs run out fast and can struggle to sink 3-1/2 inch nails.
